rules.reason: Shells out to a native binary or service (arbitrary command, gdalinfo, readpst, unrar, dwgread, strings, encode-ocr). A JS library does not ship or spawn these; Tesseract is the one opt-in exception (parser-media TesseractOcrParser, bounded and flagged unsafe). Formats with a JS route are covered by our own parsers (OutlookPSTParser, ArchiveMetadataParser for RAR, ScienceMetadataParser for DWG).
NLP/ML parsers (Lucene geo-gazetteer, GROBID journal extraction, named-entity models) need JVM-resident models or external services; not a parser concern in a JS runtime.

Vendor SDK and credential parsers. ripstream exposes VlmOcrProvider (core/vlm.ts) so a caller injects any provider; shipping per-vendor clients would put API keys and network egress in the default install.
JNI binding to Tesseract. The CLI route (TesseractOcrParser) covers OCR.
BPG is a dead format superseded by HEIF/AVIF; no maintained JS decoder, nothing to gain.
Siemens/Creo PRT is proprietary and Tika's parser only reads a header; low value, decline unless a user needs it.
ActiveMime is a macro-malware container; the useful output is the embedded VBA, which the OLE route already exposes.
application/x-tika-pst-mail-item is an internal type Tika's PSTParser feeds to itself; OutlookPSTParser emits the mail items directly.
Pack200 is a JVM-only JAR compression removed from the JDK in 14; no JS decoder.
Camera RAW variants (Adobe, Epson, Kodak, Leaf, Nikon, Olympus, Panasonic, Pentax, Samsung, Sony): low value, decline unless a user needs one. Detection still identifies them.

Macro-enabled, template, slide/slideshow, Visio and XPS types are subtypes of the three base OOXML types and Tika's CompositeParser reaches the same OOXMLParser through the MediaTypeRegistry supertype (tikajs-68os.3). Verified by a forced-type differential.
application/x-ibooks+zip is a subtype of application/epub+zip; same EpubParser through the supertype (tikajs-68os.3).
Subtype of application/vnd.ms-excel; Tika's OfficeParser reaches the Excel extractor the same way (tikajs-68os.3).
Subtype of video/mp4; same MP4Parser through the supertype (tikajs-68os.3).
Source files are plain text via the text/* registration; the oracle's text is identical except that SourceCodeParser prefixes the resource name (output-quality diff, tikajs-68os.10).
GRIB1/2 reads through netcdf-java's model, which is not portable, and the GRIB2 type is undetectable in Tika too. Owner decision pending (tikajs-68os.66).

featureNonGoals.reason: Kafka emitter/iterator needs a broker client and cluster wiring; ripstream pipes are file/HTTP streams plus caller-injected emitters.
Google Drive, Microsoft Graph and Atlassian JWT fetchers put OAuth apps, tenant IDs and network egress in the default install; a caller injects a fetcher.
Apache Ignite ConfigStore is a JVM cache/cluster product; configuration is files plus caller objects.
pf4j plugin loading is JVM class loading; ripstream configuration composes exported parser objects.
forkedJvmArgs, javaPath, useSharedServer, IPC payload size and socket/heartbeat/startup timeouts do not exist in a JS runtime; isolation has its own worker/process knobs.
tika-httpclient-commons is the JVM HTTP client stack; fetch is the platform fetch plus caller-provided transports.
/detectors and /parsers[/details] expose the JVM class graph; ripstream has the parity matrix and parser names instead.
TLS/mTLS termination is the deployer's job (spec/04); the server accepts a plain HTTP listener behind a proxy.
engines, inference and external-parser/OCR selection configure JVM services and models; ripstream exposes OCR/VLM providers as code.
grpc, plugin-roots, tika.extras.dir, xml-reader-utils, service-loader, metadata-list, allowHttp2 and fork-mode keys have no JS analogue or are decided in code.
kafka/jdbc/solr/graph iterators are JVM pipe sources; a caller supplies an iterator/stream.
PopplerRenderer, PDFBox PageDrawer and POIMetafileRenderer are page renderers; ripstream has no render SPI (tikajs-68os.9.4).
Optimaize, OpenNLP, MITLL and Lingo24 language detectors/filters need JVM models; ripstream's language detector is its own and configurable.
TikaEval and the Lingo24/Yandex/Moses/External/Joshua/Marian/RTG translators are external services or JVM integrations; callers post-process text.
comments, case-insensitive enums, ${env:} interpolation, TIKA_PASSWORD and JVM sysprops are Tika loader behaviour; ripstream config is strict JSON with explicit precedence.
Tika presets, per-request config and instantiated parse-context components are JVM server mechanics; ripstream passes options per call and a ParseContext per document.
Decision: the CLI keeps its own flags and does not emulate tika-app's; the flag mapping is documented in docs/migration.md.

GRIB2 content is netcdf-java's CDM model (dimensions/variables/attributes) built from GRIB2 IOSP and WMO/NCEP/ECMWF tables that are not in the Tika tree; Tika also cannot detect the type (registry has only application/x-grib, sent to GDALParser). A sections 0-8 reader would produce a different content model, so the port is declared a non-goal.
ISA-Tab investigation/assay types and isatab:* keys require sibling files; a single stream cannot reach them. The study file itself is implemented.
ISO 19115-3 namespaces and SIS-only model coverage are not ported; ISO 19139 is implemented.
GeoPackage R-tree virtual-table contents need SQLite's R-tree module, which sql.js does not ship; GeoPackage data tables are read.

Access table extraction needs a Jackcess-class reader of the Jet catalog, table/column definitions and compressed Unicode row data; the current stream scrape yields junk. application/x-msaccess is declared a non-goal (tikajs-68os.10.6.5).

META_EXTTEXTOUT records that carry font glyph indices, and UTF-16 text outside the normal WMF text records, are not decoded: rendering glyph indices needs the font's character map, and guessing would invent text. WMF/EMF text extraction is otherwise implemented (tikajs-68os.10.7.1).

detectionDeviations.reason: commons-compress ArchiveStreamFactory.detect (tar header checksum, cpio, ar, arj, dump, 7z) is not ported; the registry's magic covers these types and the 1201-file Tika differential has 0 mismatches. No synthetic-fixture measurement.

detectionDeviations.item: Ogg BOS pages outside the 64 KiB prefix
detectionDeviations.reason: Detection reads the 64 KiB sniffing prefix; Tika reads the whole file. Stream identification was probed from the oracle because vorbis-java is not in the Tika tree.
A bplist whose root exceeds the key budget is typed by its keys; Tika fails the parse and answers octet-stream.

detectionDeviations.item: OLE2 DIFAT chains and resource caps
detectionDeviations.reason: DIFAT chains over 130 sectors are rejected where Tika reads them; FAT 8 MiB, directory 8 MiB, mini FAT 1 MiB and mini stream 16 MiB are deliberate caps; shared entries have a 4096-revisit budget. CompObj is searched whole.
The hint-counter path is not ported; part relationships stop at a 16 MiB budget and the package is accepted.
A corrupt body after valid output loses the output; Tika keeps bytes read before the error.

Xerces drops the whole block on an immediate decode error; ripstream keeps start tags seen before the bad byte (lenient scan) and refuses for the strict POI read. Two oracle cases left out of the goldens.
XML charsets are WHATWG TextDecoder labels; a Java-only charset is refused.

detectionDeviations.item: saxes namespace checks on PI/entity names
detectionDeviations.reason: saxes' namespace-mode checks on PI targets and entity names with a colon are not replicated by xml-parse.ts, which resolves namespaces itself in linear time.
Root refinement does not get Xerces-style decoding; it uses the same WHATWG decoder as the rest.
